Troubleshooting

Choose what you see, then open the likely causes. Whispy says what went wrong in its log, one line per dictation (never its text).

tail -f ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log

Its menu also names a missing permission, with a row that opens the right System Settings pane.

Ask it what it is doing, and read the service's own output:

whispy2 send status
journalctl --user -u whispy2 -e
Pressing the trigger does nothing

No recording starts. Work through the likely causes below.

Input Monitoring is off

Whispy reads the trigger key through a listen-only event tap, which needs Input Monitoring. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring, enable Whispy V2, then restart it from the menu bar (Restart). Until then the menu says « The trigger key is not available… ».

Whispy is not running

Start it with systemctl --user start whispy2 (or the switch in the Omarchy panel), then check whispy2 send status. If it stops again, read journalctl --user -u whispy2 -e and ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log.

Open /Applications/Whispy V2.app: its waveform appears in the menu bar. If it quits again, read ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log.

The models are still loading

At first launch Whispy downloads about 1.2 GB of models. whispy2 send status shows "models_loaded":true when you can dictate.

At first launch Whispy downloads about 1.2 GB of models; the menu says Ready when you can dictate.

No X server for the key (X11)

Under X11 Whispy listens to Right Ctrl through XInput 2 on your display. If the unit started without DISPLAY, Whispy says so in a notification and in whispy2 send status. From your graphical session, run systemctl --user import-environment DISPLAY XAUTHORITY, then systemctl --user restart whispy2. Under Wayland, see the Wayland entry below.

Another key or mode is set. On macOS, press the key shown in Settings → Trigger (see trigger). In toggle mode (trigger_mode) a single press starts and a second press stops.

Recording works but no text appears

Whispy records, but nothing is typed into the focused field.

Accessibility is off

Whispy pastes (⌘V) or types through System Events, which needs Accessibility. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, enable Whispy V2 and restart it. A pasted text stays on the clipboard meanwhile: paste it by hand.

The microphone hears nothing

If Whispy says « Microphone heard nothing », the default ALSA/PulseAudio/PipeWire input is muted or wrong. Pick the right one in your sound settings (or pactl set-default-source): Whispy opens the current default at each dictation.

If Whispy says « Microphone heard nothing », the default input device is muted or wrong. Pick the right one in System Settings → Sound → Input: Whispy opens the current default at each dictation. Check that Whispy V2 is allowed in Privacy & Security → Microphone.

The text cannot be typed (Wayland)

Under Wayland Whispy types through the virtual-keyboard protocol. Hyprland and sway support it; GNOME does not. The log line of the dictation says the insertion failed.

The clip was discarded. A press under 0.3 s, a near-silent clip, or one with under 0.20 s of detected voice is ignored on purpose. ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log has one line per dictation with its outcome. See why short clips are ignored.

Text appears garbled / accents wrong

Words arrive, but characters are wrong or missing.

Keyboard layout. On macOS, keep copy_to_clipboard on (the default): the text is pasted, so accents arrive intact whatever your layout. Typing key by key depends on the layout.

Characters missing in some apps (Linux)

On Linux the text is typed one key at a time. An app that drops fast synthetic keys may lose some; dictate shorter passages, or report it with the app's name.

Whispy doesn't start / no menu bar or tray icon

Nothing shows after launch.

Another Whispy already runs

The control socket is a single-instance lock: a second Whispy finds the first one answering and exits. whispy2 send status answers if one runs; systemctl --user status whispy2 shows whether it is the service.

The control socket is a single-instance lock: a second Whispy finds the first one answering and exits. Look for its icon in the menu bar, or ask status on ~/.whispy/v2/control.sock.

It fails at start

Read journalctl --user -u whispy2 -e and ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log. Rebuild and reinstall with the one-line installer, or make reinstall from a checkout.

Read ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log. Rebuild and reinstall with the one-line installer, or make reinstall from a checkout.

First dictation is slow or fails (models)

The first dictation after launch takes long, or Whispy says the models are missing.

The models did not download

Whispy downloads its models at first launch into ~/.whispy/models (about 1.2 GB, SHA-256 checked) with curl. Without network, it retries at the next start (systemctl --user restart whispy2). The log names the file that failed.

Whispy downloads its models at first launch into ~/.whispy/models (about 1.2 GB, SHA-256 checked) and says so in a notification. Without network, it retries at the next launch. The log names the file that failed.

Linux: the trigger key does nothing under Wayland

Under Wayland no app may listen to a global key.

No compositor binding

Bind a key of your compositor to whispy2 send start on press and whispy2 send stop on release (or whispy2 send toggle). On Omarchy, run omarchy-dictation-use whispy && hyprctl reload and pick the key in the Whispy bar panel. See Install.

whispy2 is not on the binding's PATH

The installer puts whispy2 in ~/.local/bin. If your compositor's PATH lacks it, write the full path: ~/.local/bin/whispy2 send start.

Linux: the tray icon does not show

Under X11 Whispy shows a tray icon (StatusNotifierItem).

No tray host in the panel

The icon needs a StatusNotifierItem host in your panel (KDE, XFCE and most bars have one). Without it Whispy posts one notification, « Tray icon unavailable », and runs on without it: dictation still works. Under Wayland there is no tray icon; on Omarchy, the bar panel shows the state.

Still stuck? Read ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log, or open an issue.
